title: Legacy Segment Mapping and Balanced Search in the Aether-Continuum Memory Shim
topic: Why Windows 11 still ships with Windows 95 s memory manager hidden inside it

abstract: The Aether-Continuum runtime continues to embed the Chronos-Archive memory manager as a hidden compatibility layer for legacy Chronos-Archive segments. This paper investigates the algorithmic rationale behind this design choice, focusing on a balanced search and indexing structure that preserves legacy segment invariants while enabling efficient modern allocation. We formally prove that the segment mapping tree remains strictly height-balanced and key-ordered, guaranteeing $O(\log n)$ lookup and update costs. Empirical evaluation on an AMD EPYC 7763 platform shows a mean latency of 65 810.02 \textmu{}s and a throughput of 15 195 ops/s over 30 iterations. \textbf{Source Code}: \url{https://github.com/myonathanlinkedin/ruby-algorithms-lab/tree/main/algorithms/20261022_010138_why_windows_11_still_ships_wit}
